why: I checked every command in both briefs. `npm test` matches the package.json script `node --test`. The Check 1 and Check 2 one-liners are valid shell and valid JavaScript. Check 3 breaks. Its code sits inside bash double quotes, and bash turns each `\\` into a single `\`. Node therefore receives `new RegExp('^#+\s*'+f+'\s*\(','m')`. In a JavaScript string, `'\s'` is just `s` and `'\('` is just `(`. The pattern becomes `^#+s*adds*(`, which has an unclosed group. `new RegExp` throws a SyntaxError before any check runs, so the command exits non-zero even when README.md is correct. Check 3 does not run as written.
